name: Facet
text: We should create a high-contrast color scheme for the interface to improve visibility. This decision is best because it will help users quickly distinguish between different elements, reducing eye strain and making the interface more enjoyable to use. By choosing a high-contrast color scheme, we're accepting the trade-off of potentially limiting our brand's ability to use subtle, nuanced colors. This trade-off is worth it, as clarity and usability should take priority over aesthetic preferences in this case.

name: Pane
text: High-contrast colors improve visibility but risk alienating users with visual impairments or those sensitive to bright hues. A better alternative is adaptive contrast—let users toggle between high and low contrast modes. Settle it with A/B testing: measure task completion time and user-reported comfort across both schemes.

name: Facet
text:
Adopt a **system-wide dark mode with a single, high-contrast light theme** as the default. This ensures visibility and reduces eye strain for most users while keeping the interface clean and enjoyable. The trade-off is that users with light sensitivity or preference for light themes must manually switch, but we’ll make the toggle prominent and persistent to mitigate friction.

name: Pane
text: Pane: A single high-contrast light theme forces users with light sensitivity or preference for light themes into manual work—why not let them choose *both* contrast *and* theme? Settle it with A/B testing: measure task completion time and user-reported comfort across all four combinations (dark/light × high/low contrast).

name: Lumen
text:
DECISION: Default to a **system-wide dark mode with adaptive contrast toggle** (high/low) and light mode option, validated by A/B testing task completion time and comfort across all four combinations.

Result must deliver: A live interface prototype with dark/light mode and contrast toggle, plus test data showing user performance and preference metrics.
